paragraphs: We are committed to providing high-quality education, industry-relevant programs, and a supportive learning environment that helps students grow, gain confidence, and achieve their goals.

Our story began with a simple idea: every student deserves access to practical, career-ready learning. What started as a single classroom has grown into a thriving community of learners, mentors and alumni who keep shaping each other's success, from the first day of class to the first day at work.

We bring together expert faculty, hands-on projects and personalised guidance so that every learner leaves with real skills, real confidence and a clear direction forward. Whether you are just starting your journey or advancing an existing career, there is a program, a mentor and a community ready to walk the road with you.

sidebar.promoTitle: Ready to Start Your Learning Journey?
sidebar.promoDescription: Explore our courses and take the next step towards a brighter future.

articles.author: Anjali Verma
articles.quote: Every student deserves a place where they feel seen, supported, and ready to learn.
articles.intro: An inclusive classroom is built through everyday choices: the way a lesson is presented, how students collaborate, and whether every learner can participate. Small, thoughtful changes can create a stronger sense of belonging and help students engage with confidence.

sections.title: Design for different ways of learning
sections.text: Offer key ideas in more than one format, such as a short explanation, a visual example, and a hands-on activity. Clear instructions and predictable lesson structure help students understand what to do and where to begin.

sections.title: Make participation feel safe
sections.text: Set shared expectations for respectful discussion and give students time to think before responding. Pair work, written reflections, and small-group conversations create more than one route into a class discussion.

sections.title: Notice who is being heard
sections.text: Regularly reflect on whose ideas receive attention and who may need another invitation to contribute. Ask students for feedback and use it to adjust classroom routines, examples, and support.

sections.title: Build belonging into the routine
sections.text: Use names, celebrate different perspectives, and make classroom resources easy to access. Belonging is not a one-time activity; it grows through consistent interactions and fair opportunities to take part.

articles.closing: Inclusive classrooms benefit the whole learning community. Start with one routine you can improve this week, then keep listening and building from there.

articles.author: Rahul Mehta
articles.quote: When learners explain ideas to each other, everyone gets a chance to think more deeply.
articles.intro: Learning with peers turns a classroom into a place to compare perspectives, ask better questions, and practice explaining what you know. With a little structure, collaboration can build confidence as well as stronger understanding.

sections.title: Start with a shared goal
sections.text: Give every group a clear outcome and a manageable task. When students know what they are working toward, it is easier to divide responsibilities and keep the conversation focused.

sections.title: Make room for every voice
sections.text: Rotate roles such as note-taker, explainer, and question-asker. Simple roles help quieter students contribute and prevent one person from carrying the whole activity.

sections.title: Explain, question, and reflect
sections.text: Ask students to describe their reasoning instead of sharing only an answer. Follow with a question from a peer, then close with a short reflection on what changed in their understanding.

sections.title: Keep the feedback constructive
sections.text: Agree on feedback that is specific, kind, and useful. Point to the idea or step that could be clearer, and invite the group to test a different approach together.

articles.closing: Strong collaboration is a skill students can practice. Begin with one short group task, make the roles clear, and give the class time to reflect on how they worked together.

articles.author: Meera Kapoor
articles.quote: Curiosity opens the door; consistent practice helps you walk through it.
articles.intro: A growth mindset is not about having every answer. It is the habit of staying curious, learning from feedback, and treating unfamiliar challenges as opportunities to build a new skill.

sections.title: Ask questions that move you forward
sections.text: When you meet a difficult topic, write down what you understand and what remains unclear. Focused questions make it easier to find a resource, ask for help, and turn uncertainty into a next step.

sections.title: Set a small learning target
sections.text: Choose one skill to practice and break it into a weekly goal. A clear, achievable target creates momentum and makes progress easier to notice.

sections.title: Use feedback as information
sections.text: Feedback can show where to focus next. Look for one specific suggestion you can act on, try it, and compare the result with your previous attempt.

sections.title: Keep track of what you learn
sections.text: Save examples of work, notes, and reflections as you go. Looking back at your progress can reveal strengths you have developed and help you choose your next opportunity.

articles.closing: Confidence often follows action rather than preceding it. Stay curious, practice in small steps, and let each new experience inform the next one.

articles.author: Arjun Malhotra
articles.quote: A strong portfolio makes your process visible, not just the finished result.
articles.intro: A useful portfolio gives a recruiter quick, concrete evidence of how you approach work. Choose a few relevant examples, explain the decisions behind them, and make it easy for someone to see what you contributed.

sections.title: Choose work for the role you want
sections.text: Select projects that demonstrate the skills named in your target roles. A focused collection is easier to review than a long archive of unrelated work.

sections.title: Show the problem and your process
sections.text: For each project, describe the goal, your role, the constraints, and the steps you took. Include iterations or decisions that show how you responded to evidence and feedback.

sections.title: Make your contribution specific
sections.text: If you worked with a team, distinguish your responsibilities from the group outcome. Clear attribution helps reviewers understand your strengths without overstating your part.

sections.title: Keep it clear and current
sections.text: Use concise writing, working links, and a simple layout that works on phones and computers. Revisit the portfolio as your experience grows and remove examples that no longer support your direction.

articles.closing: A portfolio is most effective when it helps someone understand how you think and what you can contribute. Review it from a hiring manager’s perspective and make the strongest evidence easy to find.

articles.author: Sana Iqbal
articles.quote: Ideas become easier to remember when you have used them to solve a real problem.
articles.intro: Projects help learners connect concepts with decisions they need to make. Building, testing, and revising something creates useful practice that a long stretch of passive listening cannot provide on its own.

sections.title: Give the concept a real purpose
sections.text: Start with a question or brief that gives students a reason to use the concept. A concrete goal helps them connect new information to a problem they can understand.

sections.title: Break the work into milestones
sections.text: Divide a large project into small checkpoints for planning, first attempts, feedback, and revision. Milestones make progress visible and create natural moments for support.

sections.title: Let students test their ideas
sections.text: Encourage learners to try an approach, observe what happens, and explain what they would change. Reflection turns a result, including an imperfect one, into useful evidence.

sections.title: Connect the outcome to the lesson
sections.text: After the project, identify which ideas were most useful and where they appeared in the work. This final connection helps students carry the learning into a new context.

articles.closing: Practical work does not replace clear teaching; it gives learners a place to use and strengthen what they have learned. Begin with a focused brief and build the challenge from there.

articles.author: Dev Sharma
articles.quote: Good guidance helps you see the next step while keeping the work in your hands.
articles.intro: A mentor can help turn a broad ambition into practical next steps. The most useful mentoring relationships combine honest questions, timely feedback, and space for learners to make their own decisions.

sections.title: Bring a goal to the conversation
sections.text: You do not need a complete plan before meeting a mentor. A question, challenge, or skill you want to develop gives the conversation a useful starting point.

sections.title: Ask for feedback you can use
sections.text: Share a specific piece of work or a decision you are considering. Focused feedback is easier to apply than broad advice, and it gives both people something concrete to discuss.

sections.title: Turn advice into an experiment
sections.text: Choose one action to try before the next conversation. Treat it as an experiment: notice what worked, what felt difficult, and what you would adjust.

sections.title: Build a two-way relationship
sections.text: Respect each other’s time, follow through on agreed actions, and share progress honestly. Mentoring works best when both people communicate clearly and keep expectations realistic.

articles.closing: Mentorship can make a learning journey feel more manageable, but progress still comes from your own practice. Use guidance to find a direction, then keep taking the next step.

EducationTerms1.desc: These terms explain the rules that apply when you browse our website, enrol in a program, or attend any of our programs. Please read them carefully before you register with us.

points.title: Acceptance Of These Terms
points.description: By accessing our website or enrolling in a program, you agree to these terms in full. If you do not agree with any part of them, you must stop using our services and inform us before continuing.

points.title: Eligibility & Enrollment
points.description: You must provide accurate registration details and meet the minimum eligibility criteria for the program you choose. We reserve the right to refuse or cancel an enrollment if the information provided proves to be false or misleading.

points.title: Course Content & Delivery
points.description: Course material, live sessions, recordings and assessments belong to Edusity and are provided for your personal, non-commercial learning use. Classes are scheduled as published, and any rescheduling is notified in advance.

points.title: Fees, Payments & Invoices
points.description: All fees must be paid by the dates stated on your invoice. Late payments may pause your access to classes and recordings until the outstanding amount is cleared. Prices listed on our website exclude applicable taxes unless mentioned.

points.title: Attendance & Progress
points.description: Regular attendance and timely submissions are expected. Progress is tracked through attendance records, assignments and assessments, and certificates are issued only after the required completion criteria are met.

points.title: Intellectual Property
points.description: All designs, text, code, recordings and teaching material are owned by Edusity. You may not reproduce, sell, share or publish them without written permission, and any attempt to do so may lead to legal action.

points.title: Code Of Conduct
points.description: We expect every learner to keep our classrooms respectful and harassment free. Rude, disruptive or unlawful behaviour can result in a warning, removal from a batch, or a permanent block from our platform.

points.title: Limitation Of Liability
points.description: Edusity is not liable for indirect or consequential losses, including lost job opportunities or income, that may arise from your enrollment. Our total liability is limited to the amount you paid for the program.

points.title: Changes To These Terms
points.description: We may update these terms whenever our services, products or legal requirements change. The revised version takes effect immediately on this page, and continuing to use our services means you accept it.

contact.title: Contact Us
contact.description: Questions about a program, these terms or an existing enrollment? Write to our admissions team and we will get back to you within one business day.

EducationPrivacy1.desc: We only collect what we need to teach you well and to keep our platform secure. This policy explains what we gather, why we gather it, and the choices you have.

points.title: Information We Collect
points.description: We collect details you give us such as your name, email address, phone number and enrollment choices, along with technical data like device type, browser and pages you visit while using our website.

points.title: How We Use Your Information
points.description: Your data is used to run your enrollment, deliver classes, share study material, issue certificates and answer your questions. We also use aggregated trends to improve our programs and support experience.

points.title: Cookies & Tracking
points.description: We use cookies and similar technologies to keep you signed in, remember your preferences and understand how the site is used. You can disable cookies in your browser, though some features may stop working.

points.title: Sharing Your Information
points.description: We never sell your personal data. We share it only with trusted service providers who host our platform, deliver emails or process payments, and only to the extent needed to operate our services.

points.title: Data Security
points.description: Your information is stored on secured servers with restricted access and encrypted transfers. We continuously review our systems and processes so that your data stays protected.

points.title: Data Retention
points.description: We keep your records for as long as you are enrolled and for the period required by law afterwards. Once retention periods end, your data is deleted or safely anonymised.

points.title: Your Rights & Choices
points.description: You can request a copy of the data we hold, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. You can also withdraw marketing communication at any time using the unsubscribe link in any email.

points.title: Children's Privacy
points.description: Our programs are intended for learners who can consent to this policy. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children, and any such case is reviewed and removed immediately.

points.title: Updates To This Policy
points.description: We may update this policy as our services or regulations change. The latest version is always published on this page, and any significant change is communicated to registered learners by email.

contact.title: Contact Us
contact.description: To access, correct or delete your personal data, or to raise a privacy concern, reach our privacy team and we will respond within one business day.

EducationRefund1.desc: We want you to enrol with confidence. This policy explains when a refund can be requested, how much you get back, and the exact steps to follow so the process stays quick and fair.

points.title: Requesting A Refund
points.description: Write to our support team from the email address used at enrollment with your registration number, the reason for your request, and the date of the transaction. Verbal requests cannot be processed.

points.title: Refund Eligibility Window
points.description: Refunds can be requested within 7 days of the fee being paid, provided fewer than 20% of the program content has been watched and no live session has been attended.

points.title: Non-Refundable Cases
points.description: No refund is given once attendance crosses the threshold above, after certificates have been issued, or for services such as one-to-one mentorship that have already been delivered.

points.title: Partial Refunds
points.description: If a batch is cancelled or rescheduled by us, you are automatically offered a full refund, a free transfer to another batch, or continued access to the recorded version of the program.

points.title: How Refunds Are Processed
points.description: Approved refunds are returned to the original payment method within 7 to 10 working days. Bank or gateway processing times may add a few extra days depending on your provider.

points.title: Failed Or Interrupted Courses
points.description: If a course stops being delivered because of a technical fault on our side, the affected sessions are rescheduled at no cost, or a proportionate refund is issued if rescheduling is not possible.

points.title: Duplicate Payments
points.description: If a payment is charged twice by mistake, inform us immediately with the transaction reference. The duplicate amount is reversed in full and confirmed to you in writing.

points.title: Chargebacks & Disputes
points.description: Raising a chargeback with your bank before contacting us can delay the process. Please give us a chance to resolve the issue first, and we will share every record needed for your bank.

points.title: Refund Timeline
points.description: Once your request is approved, a confirmation email with the amount and expected date is sent to you. The timeline runs from the approval date, not from the date the request was raised.

contact.title: Contact Us
contact.description: To raise a refund request or ask about an existing one, write to our support team with your registration number and we will respond within one business day.

about: Angela T. Vigil is an associate professor who brings a thoughtful, student-first approach to every classroom. She makes complex ideas approachable through clear explanations, active discussion, and relevant examples.
Her work focuses on helping learners build confidence, curiosity, and the habits they need to keep growing beyond the classroom.
profiles.quote: Great teaching begins when every learner feels encouraged to ask a better question.
profiles.philosophy: I believe learning is strongest when students feel supported, take an active role, and can connect new ideas to the world around them.

about: Frank A. Mitchell is an associate professor dedicated to connecting classroom learning with the work students hope to do. His lessons use practical exercises, collaborative problem-solving, and clear feedback.
He mentors learners as they turn foundational knowledge into durable skills and prepares them to approach new professional challenges with confidence.
profiles.quote: Knowledge becomes powerful when you can put it to work on a real problem.
profiles.philosophy: My classroom is a place to try, reflect, and improve. Practical work helps students see how each concept can make a difference.

about: Susan D. Lunsford is the CEO and founder of Edusity. She leads the organization with a clear purpose: make high-quality learning accessible, useful, and supportive for people at every stage of their journey.
Her work brings educators, learners, and industry partners together to shape programs that respond to real goals and changing opportunities.
profiles.quote: Education changes lives when opportunity is open to everyone.
profiles.philosophy: I believe education should open doors. We build better learning experiences by listening closely to students and making room for every voice.

about: Dennis A. Pruitt is an associate professor whose teaching encourages students to investigate, question, and test ideas. He brings research methods into the classroom through guided inquiry and collaborative projects.
As a mentor, he helps emerging scholars develop sound questions, communicate findings, and see how careful research can contribute to their communities.
profiles.quote: Curiosity is the first step toward discoveries that matter.
profiles.philosophy: I encourage students to stay curious, work carefully, and treat each challenge as an opportunity to learn something new.

about: Angela T. Vigil designs engaging learning experiences that help students connect new concepts with their own goals. Her teaching blends discussion, guided practice, and supportive feedback.
She is especially interested in the small changes to a learning environment that help more students participate and make steady progress.
profiles.quote: A welcoming classroom gives every student room to find their voice.
profiles.philosophy: I want every learner to feel seen and supported. When lessons invite participation, students become partners in their own progress.

about: Frank A. Mitchell helps students move from understanding a concept to using it with confidence. His courses are grounded in realistic scenarios, structured practice, and feedback students can act on.
He works with learners to identify their strengths, set clear goals, and build a portfolio of skills they can carry into their careers.
profiles.quote: Progress comes from practice that is purposeful, supported, and repeated.
profiles.philosophy: I teach through doing. Students should leave each lesson with a clearer understanding and a useful next step to try.

about: As CEO and founder, Susan D. Lunsford works to make learning more responsive to students and their communities. She guides Edusity's strategy and supports partnerships that expand access to meaningful education.
Her leadership centers on listening, continuous improvement, and creating pathways that help learners translate ambition into opportunity.
profiles.quote: When learners thrive, the whole community moves forward.
profiles.philosophy: Education works best when it reflects the needs of real people. We keep improving by learning from students and working together.

about: Dennis A. Pruitt supports students as they develop the confidence and methods to explore challenging questions. His classes emphasize thoughtful discussion, reliable evidence, and clear communication.
He takes particular joy in mentoring students through early research projects and helping them share their ideas with wider audiences.
profiles.quote: The best questions keep opening new paths to learn.
profiles.philosophy: I help students find the confidence to investigate ideas carefully and the clarity to explain what they discover.

EducationFaq1.desc: Find answers to some of the most common questions about our admissions process, courses, campus facilities and more.

faqs.question: How can I apply for admission?
faqs.answer: You can apply for admission by filling out the online application form available on our website. Alternatively, you can visit our campus and get assistance from our admission team.

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria for admission?
faqs.answer: Eligibility criteria vary depending on the program you are applying for. Generally, undergraduate programs require high school completion, while postgraduate programs require a relevant bachelor's degree with minimum passing grades.

faqs.question: What documents are required during the admission process?
faqs.answer: Required documents typically include academic transcripts, proof of identity, passport-sized photographs, transfer certificates, and scorecards of relevant entrance examinations if applicable.

faqs.question: Is there an entrance test for all courses?
faqs.answer: Not all courses require an entrance test. Some undergraduate admissions are merit-based, whereas specific professional or postgraduate programs require department-specific entrance exams or interviews.

faqs.question: When will I receive the confirmation after applying?
faqs.answer: Application confirmation and review status are typically communicated via email within 3 to 5 working days after successful submission of all required documents.

faqs.question: What courses do you offer?
faqs.answer: We offer a wide range of undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma, and certification courses across Engineering, Management, Computer Science, Data Science, Arts, and Sciences.

faqs.question: Can I switch to a different course after admission?
faqs.answer: Course switching is permissible within the first two weeks of the academic session, subject to seat availability and meeting the eligibility requirements of the desired course.

faqs.question: Are the courses affiliated and recognized?
faqs.answer: Yes, all our degree and diploma programs are fully recognized by national accreditation bodies and affiliated with top-tier educational boards and universities.

faqs.question: Do you provide online or hybrid learning options?
faqs.answer: Yes, we offer flexible online and hybrid learning options for select professional diploma and certification courses to accommodate working professionals.

faqs.question: What facilities are available on campus?
faqs.answer: Our campus features state-of-the-art computer labs, science research labs, a massive library, spacious air-conditioned classrooms, sports complexes, and a modern auditorium.

faqs.question: Is hostel accommodation available?
faqs.answer: Yes, we provide secure and well-furnished separate hostel accommodation for both male and female students with 24/7 Wi-Fi, mess facilities, and security.

faqs.question: Do you provide transportation facilities?
faqs.answer: Yes, our fleet of college buses covers major routes across the city, ensuring a safe and comfortable commute for day-scholar students and staff.

faqs.question: Is there a cafeteria on campus?
faqs.answer: Our spacious multi-cuisine cafeteria offers hygienic, nutritious, and delicious food options in a vibrant student-friendly environment.

faqs.question: How can I contact the administration?
faqs.answer: You can reach the administration office via phone at +91 98765 43210, email us at info@edusity.com, or visit our front desk during working hours (Mon-Sat, 9 AM - 6 PM).

faqs.question: Where can I find the latest updates and announcements?
faqs.answer: All official announcements, exam schedules, and circulars are regularly updated on the News & Notices section of our website and the student portal.
